# Bichir: A prehistoric addition to your aquarium
## How long do Bichirs live?
Bichirs tend to live much longer compared to your average aquarium specimens and ten to fifteen years in captivity can be expected. The _Polypteridae_ lifespan depends greatly on the owner’s attentiveness and conditions of the aquarium.
For an attentive owner who provides exactly what the Bichir needs, these unique specimens can live for a significant amount of time, even as long as twenty years.

...

## How big do Bichir get?
The average size of a _Polypteridae_ is between 1' and 2-1/2' in length, depending on the type of Bichir you get.

## What size tank should I get for a Bichir?
The minimum recommended tank size for a Bichir is 90 gallons. While many have reared these species in smaller tanks, the physical attributes of the Bichir support the use of a larger tank for housing them.
Bichirs are highly active and when fully grown will require a tank that provides them with ample room to move.
